injuried.emotions: 25-40 years old, self-confident, a bit blase

dialogOption.texten: 911, what's your emergency?
I'm calling from the Charlie Herald editorial office. We've received a death threat again.
I'm calling from the Washington Scoffers editorial office. We've received a death threat again.
{NAME?}What is your name?
I am Kate Barne.
{AGAIN?}Again? So you had this happen before?
{WHY WOULD YOU GET IT?} Ma'am, do you have any idea why someone would be sending threats to your organization?
{HOW?}How did you receive the threat?
I don't remember exactly. Maybe two weeks ago? We're political journalists, we're used to it. According to our policy we report all threats to 911... but in my opinion it's usually unnecessary.
Probably someone doesn't like our writing style!
{EXCUSE ME?}Excuse me?
{IT IS SERIOUS} Ma'am, you shouldn't joke about these things. You could be in real danger.
{ADDRESS} What's the address for your office?
943 West Place
20 Fortigs Boulevard
223A Osmond Street

Honestly, I'm not surprised. You know... journalism is about printing what someone else does not want printed. Yesterday, we wrote about a suspicious suicide, two days ago about terrorists among illegal immigrants...
The letter came to our office. Who send paper letters these days?. Usually, we receive death threats by e-mail.
Do you want me to read it?
{YES} Yes, please.
{NO!} No! Do not touch the letter.
Oh my... I already did it... Do you think there could be a poison on it?
{DECONTAMINATION} I am sending emergency services to put the office in quarantine and decontaminate it. Just wait for them and everything will be fine.
{LOOK FOR POISON} It's possible. I want you to check the envelope.
Em... wait a second . . . . . . . . . . . .
Ok, I have it.
{SLOWLY OPEN}Great. Now, slowly open the envelope and look into it. Is there any powder or another substance?
Jesus... I see some white powder. And it smells odd. Oh shit! Please send the ambulance right away! I think I've just exposed myself to whatever's in this envelope.
{PUT IT AWAY!} Put it away immediately and don't spill it!
Will I die? Please, help me...
{WHO ELSE TOUCHED IT?} Was there anybody else in your office who touched the letter?
Yes, I showed it to my editor-in-chief. He said he felt a little sick, so he lay down in his office. I think he's asleep. Should I wake him up?
{WAIT FOR HELP}No, stay where you are and wait for the help.
{WAKE HIM UP}Yes. Go to his office now, check him, see if he's conscious.
Ok, I'm going.
Greg, are you okay? Greg!
I can't wake him up. Please, tell me what to do...
{CHECK HIS PULSE}Check his pulse.
{IS HE BREATHING?}Is he breathing?
Yes, I can feel it!
Wait... yes, he is breathing.
It's rather short: 'Curiosity killed the cat, do you have nine lives, too? You better have, because today you will lose the first one'
It's rather short: 'Curiosity is a fatal sin'
{I'LL SEND THE POLICE} Okay, I'll have officers attend and look into it.
{I WON'T SEND THE POLICE} It doesn't sound like something serious. If the threats happen again, please report them. For now, you should remain calm and be careful.
Yep, I agree. I have to report it, because of our company's policy, but it's probably nothing. Thanks for your time, bye!
I don't think that is necessary, but it's your call. I will wait for them with the letter.
I'll wait. Please come as soon as it possible...
Are you there?

reportElement.texten: Decontamination was performed, which saved a possible pathogen from spreading.
An editorial office has received a death threat letter. The letter contained a dangerous poison.
The operator should have sent the emergency services and put the office in quarantine.
The operator told the caller to check the letter, which confirmed presence of toxic powder, but also exposed the journalist for the effect of the poison.
The office was put in quarantine. Police found ricin inside the envelope.
The operator should have put office in quarantine and decontaminate it.
The police have examined the letter. It will serve as an evidence
